text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Multiple serving-runtime containers restarting across gpu-shard-2 (gpu-12, gpu-15). Symptoms: CUDA OOM, host OOM, and occasional kernel panic traces. Escalating to #incidents.

jamie (oncall): Noted. Looking at alerts. What's the faulty signal?

taylor: Traces point to paged-attention allocator failing to coalesce free pages under sustained long-context workloads. Fragmentation ratios hitting ~0.9.

yana: Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serving/runtime?panel=allocs&cluster=gpu-shard-2  memory climb over 48h then sharp series of allocation failures starting ~10m ago.

priya: Customer impact: 4 Dedicated customers reporting 5xxs and slow responses. CS queued a notification. No PII exposure.

jamie (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable aggressive kv-eviction on affected shard 2) reduce per-worker max_concurrent_requests 3) enable allocator background-defrag (if safe) 4) cordon any node showing kernel OOM traces. I'll coordinate.

yana: Running probe: `ssh gpu-12 sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -n 500 --no-pager` then `kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide | grep gpu-12`. Found repeated error snippets:```
[2026-03-15T05:01:02Z] allocator: paged_alloc size=8192 frag=0.91 free_run=0 -> cannot satisfy contiguous
[2026-03-15T05:01:03Z] runtime: kv_cache: active=1.2M stale=0 evict_watermark=0
[2026-03-15T05:01:03Z] cuda: cuCtxCreate -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (0x1)
```

priya: Eviction heuristic apparently didn't trigger because stale metric was near zero  cache looked "active" but highly fragmented. We might need a fragmentation-driven eviction trigger.

jamie (oncall): Agreed. For now: taylor, flip `kv_eviction_aggressiveness=high` on shard gpu-shard-2. yana, reduce `worker_concurrency` to 2 for high-memory pool. Priya, coordinate CS message update.

taylor: Kicking change via infra API: `POST /admin/pools/gpu-shard-2/config {"kv_eviction_aggressiveness":"high"}`. Deploy id: cfg-2812345678-a.

deploy-bot: Config change cfg-2812345678-a applied to gpu-shard-2 (rolling, 2min window).

yana: Concurrency reduced on high-memory pool. Proxy now returns 429 for requests > 20000 tokens. Implemented with: `proxyctl rule add --pool high-memory --max-tokens 20000 --reason "incident"`.

priya: CS sent update: "We're investigating elevated error rates for large-context workloads. Temporary limits applied to protect stability. We'll follow up with ETA."

taylor: Running a forced compaction on kv-store node: `kvctl compact --host kv-gs-02 --slots 15000`. Initial compaction freed ~11k slots, frag ratio dropped 0.92 -> 0.66 on kv-gs-02.

sre-bot: Note: kernel OOM recorded on gpu-15 at 05:07:21 UTC. PID 42890 (serving-runtime) killed. Dumping /proc/42890/maps to /var/incidents/2812345678/maps.

jamie (oncall): Good. We're seeing improvement on gpu-12 and kv-gs-02. But gpu-15 still has pinned host memory ~94%. I'm cordoning gpu-15 and will drain it for a restart.

yana: While cordoning, I see one pod crash with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` referencing a pointer near the tail of KV buffer. Suspect allocator staleness interacting with GPU paging.

priya: Customer note: One enterprise tenant requested dedicated fallback nodes. Engineering: can we offer a temporary reservation?

jamie (oncall): We can spin up a reserved node set but it will take ~12-15min. Prioritize stabilization first. If they insist, CS can offer credits.

taylor: Observed that retry storms are amplifying memory churn. Adding a short leaky-bucket at gateway for this shard: `gatewayctl set-rate gpu-shard-2 --burst 30 --rate 10r/s`.

deploy-bot: Gateway rate-limiter change applied. Monitoring.

yana: After drain+restart of gpu-15, host memory reclaimed to 42% and runtime restarted cleanly. One model load failed due to `cuBLAS init` error then recovered after pod restart.

sre-bot: Captured core file: `/var/crash/serving-runtime.core.42890` on gpu-15. Archiving to s3: `s3://incidents/2812345678/serving-runtime.core.42890`

jamie (oncall): Great. Current status: fragmentation cluster avg down from 0.89 -> 0.61, eviction rates increased, retries limited. Still monitoring for 30m. If fragmentation creeps >0.8 we will trigger cluster-wide temporary throttle for long-context jobs.

priya: CS reports two customers still experiencing intermittent 503s. They're asking for a definitive root cause ETA. Suggested response: "We're stabilizing memory fragmentation in the allocator; we'll provide a technical postmortem in 48 hours." Approve?

jamie (oncall): Approve. Send it.

taylor: I'm opening a ticket for runtime team to consider: 1) fragmentation-triggered eviction 2) background-defrag when frag>0.8 3) better observability for per-model KV footprint. Ticket: `RT-3592`.

sre-bot: Suggested short-term change flagged: enable conservative background-defrag on high-memory pools only. Risk: brief CPU/GPU throughput drop during defrag.

jamie (oncall): Deploying conservative background-defrag to high-memory pool as experiment: `POST /admin/pools/high-memory/experiment {"bg_defrag":"conservative"}`. Keep it rolling on a 2-node canary.

deploy-bot: Canary for bg-defrag started (nodes gpu-12,gpu-21). Monitoring 5m.

yana: Canary looks OK: no visible latency spike, fragmentation on canary nodes down another ~0.05.

priya: CS queued follow-up: customers notified of temporary limits and expected full restoration in 60-90 minutes.

jamie (oncall): Handoff: I'm staying for next update, but priya, prepare incident summary for postmortem intake. Taylor, tag eng-runtime to prioritize a hotfix for fragmentation detection. If this stabilizes over 60m, we'll close and schedule RCA.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (eviction aggressiveness up, proxy limits, background-defrag canary). Partial recovery noted. Next update in 30m or on status change.

priya: Noted. Archiving logs: `tar czf /var/incidents/2812345678/logs.tgz /var/log/serving/* && aws s3 cp /var/incidents/2812345678/logs.tgz s3://incidents/2812345678/`.

yana: Followups: collect `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv` across cluster every 1m for 1h and attach to RCA.

taylor: Created PR for more aggressive eviction heuristics: `github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4920` title "eviction: trigger on fragmentation thresholds" marked as candidate.

jamie (oncall): Thanks all. Leaving channel open; next status at +30m unless there's a regression.
